Subject: Redwood Dedicated - discovery recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk us through Aurora Finance's inference needs. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed or that needs correction.

Summary of pain points
- Unpredictable latency and tail p99 spikes during batch settlement windows that impact UX and downstream reconciliation workflows.
- Need for strong data isolation and controls (PII/financial data) to meet internal audit and regulator expectations.
- Current in-house infra struggles to hit predictable throughput during peak CPS (concurrent prediction spikes).

Current stack / constraints
- Model: mixing several open LLMs for summarization and entity extraction (on-prem fine-tuned LLMs).
- Serving: k8s with Triton today, autoscale rules tuned for CPU/GPU but inconsistent during traffic surges.
- Security: SOC2+ evidence required; key management via in-house HSM.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable baseline throughput of ~500 req/s (avg) with p95 < 100ms and p99 < 150ms for text-generation paths.
- Ability to reserve GPU pools for isolation and predictable TPS during SLAs (monthly reserved capacity).
- Autoscaling/burst: handle 2x peak for 10-20 minutes without degradation (canary plan for rollouts).
- Auditability: KMS integration + logs for request tracing, retention 1 year.

Recommended next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Rafael (solutions engineer) to validate sequence-length distributions, KV cache opportunities, and burst profile. Rafael can run a lightweight perf test against a staging workload.
2) Share SOC2 questionnaire and SOW draft for legal/procurement review (I attached a draft SOW we typically start from).
3) Pricing model: we will propose a reserved capacity quote (monthly) + overage policy for bursts; will aim to align with your procurement window in Nov.
4) Proposed timeline: perf test in 1 week, SOW & pricing by end of next week, pilot (canary) in mid-Nov.

Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.pdf (stub)

If this looks right, I’ll loop Rafael into a technical call and we can propose calendar slots.

Thanks —

Marissa, thanks for the detailed write-up — that's a great summary and matches what we discussed. A few follow-ups / clarifications from our side: 

Clarifications
- Baseline: the 500 req/s is correct as a near-term target; long-term we expect to ramp to ~1.2k req/s over 6 months as we onboard more products.
- Burst profile: bursts typically last 10-15 minutes but can reach 2.5x baseline during settlement windows.
- Security: SOC2 evidence is a must; we will share the questionnaire (attached). We also have a request to see KMS integration options and key rotation policy.
- Budget: procurement has signaled a desire to cap monthly spend; can you provide a committed capacity price vs. pay-as-you-go comparison?

Next steps from Aurora
- I'll share the SOC2 spreadsheet with the specific evidence fields we need (attached: aurora-soc2-questions.xlsx).
- We are available for a technical deep dive on Wed or Thu morning PST.
- Legal will want to review the SOW + standard PO terms.

Thanks — I'll coordinate internal availability and confirm a time for the technical call.
